spans.text:
Before we begin Pesukei D'Zimrah with its opening brachah of Baruch She'amar, we say this chapter of Tehillim that David HaMelech created for the eventual Chanukas HaBayis—inauguration of the Beis Hamikdash—which interestingly enough, he was not allowed to build!

How is this relevant to us today, and what does it have to do with Pesukei D'Zimrah and the Beis Hamikdash?

This chapter discusses the difficulties (physical, emotional, and spiritual) that David HaMelech faced in his lifetime, and his belief that Hashem could and would pull him through it all. He also expresses his belief that eventually his labors would bear fruit (the Beis Hamikdash would be built), even though he knew it was ordained by Hashem that he would not live to see it! Yet he did the best he could with the struggles Hashem sent his way and thanked Hashem for all he did accomplish.

We too have no idea whether Hashem will allow us to see the end results of all our hard work! Yet we will now say Pesukei D'Zimrah and thank Hashem for all He has done and proclaim our belief that He controls all the circumstances in our lives. We will say the Shema and proclaim our loyalty to His Torah through thick and thin, and based on that, we will ask Him to give us the things we think we need in order to accomplish our mission (Shemoneh Esrei). And we do this with joy and faith even though we do not know whether we will merit to see it all to fruition or not!

Importantly, the Malbim says that this chapter really refers to our body—also a mini Beis Hamikdash—a physical thing that we fill with kedushah and use to fulfill our mission. And, like the real Beis Hamikdash, it must be treated with respect and sanctity!

Some find Pesukei D'Zimrah "annoying"—all this praising of Hashem strikes them as strange. "What does He need that for?" Of course, Hashem doesn't need our praises—we need to praise Him! For an explanation of this crucial idea, see the Introduction to Birkas Ha'mazon on page 119.

Much of Pesukei D'Zimrah is made up of Tehillim, which is poetry. The nuances and beauty of the various paragraphs are too easily lost, which is why some people have the unfortunate "custom" of saying just Baruch She'amar, Ashrei, and Yishtabach. Here, we will try to convey the point of each part, but this can never do justice to the depth, beauty, and lofty spiritual ideas David HaMelech wove into every sentence. Still, any improvement counts!

—A song composed by David HaMelech to be used in the eventual dedication of the Beis Hamikdash. Hashem—I praise You because You have raised me up from the depths of all my difficulties—and You did not let my enemies (real or imagined) triumph over me. I called out to You and You healed me; You brought me back up when I was down. We should always be singing Your praises because Your "anger" is only for a moment—and its purpose is really to improve our lives! Though בְּעֶרֶב—in "dark times" (when we are in pain) we do not understand the purpose of our pain, we are
"in the morning" (when all is clear), we will be joyful.

When all is calm and my body healthy, I think that state is natural and will last forever. But I know that it is You, Hashem, Who keeps me strong. If You would chas v'shalom "turn away from me"—all would fall apart.

Therefore, I turn to You for help; it is to You I call out and proclaim: "My goal is to accomplish the mission You gave me." Therefore, I need Your (material and emotional) support to allow me to do that!

So many times You turn my difficulties into growth opportunities (even though I do not always realize that at the moment)—all in order for me to accomplish my mission. Hashem Who takes care of me—in all circumstances I will praise You!

(The person saying Kaddish proclaims our hope that) soon, in our lifetime, the entire world, which Hashem created precisely according to His Will, will recognize Hashem as the Source of all and will see the sanctity, perfection, and purpose of all He has done.
(We all enthusiastically respond:) Absolutely correct! May everyone (including me!), everywhere, and forever, see that all His actions are great and deserving of praise!

(The person saying Kaddish then points out that) in reality, the true greatness and power of Hashem far exceeds any praises that we mere humans could say. And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely correct!
(The person saying Kaddish requests:) May there be abundant peace, that comes from Heaven, and life, upon us and upon all of Bnei Yisrael. And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely, we agree!
(The person saying Kaddish requests:) May He Who makes peace in the Heavens bring about peace upon us and upon all of Bnei Yisrael! And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely, we agree!

בָּרוּךְ שֶׁאָמַר—The Source of everything (Hashem) spoke and created the entire universe; He makes decrees and fulfills them; He shows mercy to all His creatures (giving them opportunities to correct their mistakes); He rewards those who fear Him; and He is Eternal (there is Divine justice, even though as limited humans we cannot always see it). He redeems and rescues us (personally from our own physical and mental traumas; and as a nation throughout our history); to sum it all up—בָּרוּךְ שְׁמוֹ—His Presence is the Source for everything! בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; אֱלֹהֵינוּ—You take care of us; מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם—and You rule the entire world; the All-powerful (yet at the same time) merciful Father Who is praised by His entire nation. With the Tehillim of David HaMelech Your servant, we too will now (in the upcoming sections of Pesukei D'Zimrah) sing Your praises and affirm Your rulership over us. יָחִיד חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים—You are the Sole Giver of life to the entire universe; the King Whose actions are praised eternally (for we believe that they are all fair and just). בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מֶלֶךְ מְהֻלָּל בַּתִּשְׁבָּחוֹת—the King Who is praised by all (including me!).

הוֹדוּ—Even though I am now going to personally praise Hashem for all He does, and focus on His power in nature and history (which will then lead me to personally accept His sovereignty on myself—the Shema), really the entire world should acknowledge the power of Hashem and praise Him. Hashem chose our Avos and Imahos, turned them into a great nation and miraculously gave us Eretz Yisrael (and we are the center of world attention). No power throughout history has been able to destroy us. (Our very centrality on the world stage is itself the greatest proof of Hashem's power and our special bond with Him.) For that we praise Hashem, and it provides us with a sense of security and joy.

שִׁירוּ לַיהוָה כָּל הָאָרֶץ, בַּשְּׂרוּ מִיּוֹם אֶל יוֹם יְשׁוּעָתוֹ—We await the day (when Mashiach comes) and the entire world will acknowledge the truth, and see the power of Hashem in history and in the beauty and majesty of nature. And the entire Creation will proclaim:
Praise and thank Hashem, for ALL that He does is good (even though now it is hard for us to see that); His kindness and care for us is eternal.

Redeem us from our (physical and spiritual) galus so that we may serve You in the Beis Hamikdash; forgive our sins; and raise our esteem among the nations. We place our complete faith and trust in You that You will save us from all misfortunes and give us the ability to fulfill our mission to the world. Just as You took us out of Egypt (and chose us as Your nation), we are confident that You will grant all our requests.
Happy and fortunate are we, the nation (Bnei Yisrael) that has all this glorious history and great mission.
Happy and fortunate are we, the nation (Bnei Yisrael) that has Hashem as our personal God Who takes care of us.

(Even though life is dark for me now, but) I have complete trust in Your kindness; יָגֵל לִבִּי בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ—(I am confident that in the end when all becomes clear) my heart will rejoice because of Your salvation.
(And I am so confident that all is for the good, that right now—even in my darkness) I will sing to Hashem, because I know that all He does to me is for my good.

מִזְמוֹר לְתוֹדָה—A song of thanksgiving (and/or, a song sung when the Korban Todah was brought in the Beis Hamikdash): הָרִיעוּ לַיהֹוָה כָּל הָאָרֶץ—The entire earth should call out to Hashem in thanks. עִבְדוּ אֶת יְהֹוָה בְּשִׂמְחָה—Serve Hashem with simchah—happiness and peace of mind! בֹּאוּ לְפָנָיו בִּרְנָנָה—The way to get close to Him is through gladness! דְּעוּ כִּי יְהֹוָה הוּא אֱלֹהִים—Know that Hashem is THE One Who takes care of us (and/or, the י-ה-ו-ה—the Name that represents God's attribute of mercy, is the same as אלהים—the Name that represents God's attribute of Justice—since Hashem's judgments of us are all for our benefit!). הוּא עָשָׂנוּ—He created us, וְלוֹ אֲנַחְנוּ עַמּוֹ וְצֹאן מַרְעִיתוֹ—and we Bnei Yisrael are His unique nation, which He shepherds throughout history. בֹּאוּ שְׁעָרָיו בְּתוֹדָה חֲצֵרֹתָיו בִּתְהִלָּה—We enter the Beis Hamikdash (today, we enter our mini Beis Hamidkash—our shuls and homes) with thanksgiving; הוֹדוּ לוֹ בָּרְכוּ שְׁמוֹ—praise Hashem for all that He does for us. כִּי טוֹב יְהֹוָה לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ—For Hashem is the sole absolute Good, His kindness is constant and daily in our lives (even when we cannot see it); וְעַד דֹּר וָדֹר אֱמוּנָתוֹ—and His Presence is consistent in all generations, past and future.
יְהִי כְבוֹד—May the Presence of Hashem be felt and seen clearly in the world; (that way it will be easier for us to act appropriately) and thus Hashem will be pleased with us—His creations.

From the East to the West—the entire world, the Heavens and the earth and all the nations proclaim the glory of Hashem and His absolute and eternal rulership over "nature" and the course of world history—from the beginning of time till the end of days.

רַבּוֹת מַחֲשָׁבוֹת בְּלֶב אִישׁ—Humans have many plans, thoughts and intentions; וַעֲצַת יְהֹוָה הִיא תָקוּם—but in the end, only the plan of Hashem will prevail. The "plan" Hashem has for history is eternal and spans all generations (which is why we have difficulty grasping its entirety).
כִּי בָחַר יְהֹוָה בְּצִיּוֹן, אִוָּהּ לְמוֹשָׁב לוֹ—Hashem has chosen Eretz Yisrael as His special land, and us, Bnei Yisrael, as His (סְגֻלָּתוֹ) special treasure.
כִּי לֹא יִטֹּשׁ יְהֹוָה עַמּוֹ—and He will never destroy Bnei Yisrael or abandon His land.

וְהוּא רַחוּם יְכַפֵּר עָוֹן וְלֹא יַשְׁחִית—(Even if we mess up,) He will forgive our sins, give us another chance; יְהֹוָה הוֹשִׁיעָה, הַמֶּלֶךְ יַעֲנֵנוּ בְיוֹם קָרְאֵנוּ—Hashem, please (continue) to save us and answer our tefillos whenever we call out to You.

Happy are those who (wherever they are) are living in the house of Hashem (living a meaningful and spiritually growing life); עוֹד יְהַלְלוּךָ סֶּלָה—they will constantly praise You (since they see all the circumstances of their life as opportunities for growth).

הָעָם שֶׁכָּכָה לּוֹ—Happy and fortunate are we, the nation (Bnei Yisrael) that has all this (glorious history and great mission); אַשְׁרֵי הָעָם שֶׁיהֹוָה אֱלֹהָיו—happy and fortunate are we, the nation (Bnei Yisrael) that Hashem as our personal God Who takes care of us.

A song of praise by David HaMelech (תהילים קמה): אֲרוֹמִמְךָ אֱלוֹהַי הַמֶּלֶךְ—I will exalt and revere You (since I realize that the essence of Hashem as my personal God and Ruler of the entire universe is way beyond our human comprehension); וַאֲבָרְכָה שִׁמְךָ—and (at the same time) I thank You (in the following verses) for all that You have done and will do (for me personally and for our nation); לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד—since the beginning of time and until the end of days.

(You are the Source of everything that happens to me each and every day, and) I thank You for it all (even though some of those things are hard to understand); נַאֲהַלְלָה שִׁמְךָ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד—and in the end of days, I will truly praise You (as all becomes clear).

(As much as we will thank and praise Hashem, and proclaim) Hashem is "great" and is "extremely praised"; וְלִגְדֻלָּתוֹ אֵין חֵקֶר—(the truth is that) the greatness of Hashem is beyond our real comprehension ("the more you know, the more you realize that you don't know").
Each generation will praise Your actions to the next generation; וּגְבוּרֹתֶיךָ יַגִּידוּ—and will tell them of Your (miraculous) mighty deeds (that they experienced).
I will discuss (with everyone) the beauty of Your natural world; וְדִבְרֵי נִפְלְאוֹתֶיךָ אָשִׂיחָה—as well as speak of Your wonders (which are beyond our comprehension).

(Says David HaMelech:) Others (are impressed by and) speak of Your miraculous wonders; וּגְדוּלָּתְךָ אֲסַפְּרֶנָּה—but I speak of Your constant chessed and daily greatness (which is no less miraculous)!

They (one generation passing down the heritage to the next) will speak of Your abundant goodness (notwithstanding whatever difficulties that generation may have endured); וְצִדְקָתְךָ יְרַנֵּנוּ—and they sing about Your generosity (that Hashem blesses us with more than the strict letter of the law would dictate).

Hashem is gracious (giving us goodness more than we deserve) and merciful; (and that is apparent in the fact that He is) אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וּגְדָל חָסֶד—slow to anger, and thus shows His true greatness through His abundant chessed.

Hashem is good to all (of humanity—even those who have not yet lived up to their potential); וְרַחֲמָיו עַל כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו—and His mercy extends to all that He has created (even the smallest of the animal world).

All of Your creations will thank You (for Your goodness); וַחֲסִידֶיךָ יְבָרְכוּכָה—but Your righteous ones (who have used their God-given gifts to increase sanctity and goodness into the world) will draw increased energy from You, the Source of all blessing, and in turn (by their good deeds) they will increase blessing in Your world.

They (Your righteous ones) will discuss the glory of Your Kingdom (the Hand of Hashem as seen in the beauty and complexity of the natural world—which we take for granted, and therefore must be discussed a lot); וּגְבוּרָתְךָ יְדַבֵּרוּ—and they will also tell of Your mighty open miracles (which are clear and do not need much discussion).

But when they speak to the common man, first they tell about Hashem's might and open miracles (since that is easy for people to see); וּכְבוֹד הֲדַר מַלְכוּתוֹ—and (from the open miracles they) then explain to the common people how to see the Hand of Hashem in the daily miracles of "nature."

Your Kingship is over all the "worlds" (the multitude of spiritual spheres and worlds that are beyond our comprehension); and וּמֶמְשַׁלְתְּךָ בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר—Your rulership spans eternity and governs each unique generation (in its own special role in Your master plan, all of which is also beyond our human comprehension).

—סוֹמֵךְ יְהֹוָה לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים (Though Hashem is "busy" ruling over the entire universe and eternity, yet still He looks after each and every one of us constantly, and) He supports every individual who has fallen (spiritually or emotionally); וְזוֹקֵף לְכָל הַכְּפוּפִים—and He helps every person who is bent over (from his struggles) to get up (and continue his climb toward personal perfection).

—עֵינֵי כֹל אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּ (Therefore) every creature, from the smallest to the greatest, looks to You with hope (that You will take care of them); וְאַתָּה נוֹתֵן לָהֶם אֶת אָכְלָם בְּעִתּוֹ—and You do give each one its (physical, spiritual, and emotional) sustenance—just at the time they really need it.

—פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ (Thus we proclaim emphatically that) You open Your Hand; וּמַשְׂבִּיעַ לְכָל חַי רָצוֹן—and give each person what they need in order to be satisfied. (If you feel you are not getting what you need—focus on the next verse…)

—צַדִּיק יְהֹוָה בְּכָל דְּרָכָיו All that Hashem does is just and righteous (even though as humans it does not always appear that way to us); וְחָסִיד בְּכָל מַעֲשָׂיו—and He applies that justice with great kindness.

—קָרוֹב יְהֹוָה לְכָל קֹרְאָיו (In truth,) Hashem is close to all who call to Him; לְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָאֻהוּ בֶאֱמֶת—but one must call out to Hashem with emes—honesty and sincerity. (This means that (1) you do not say one thing in your tefillos but then by your actions distance yourself from Hashem; (2) in general, whenever you speak it is with honesty, i.e., you are a "man of your word" and sincere; and (3) it is clear from your actions that you are sincere in your requests from Hashem, since you are doing whatever you personally can do to achieve those goals.)

רְצוֹן יְרֵאָיו יַעֲשֶׂה—He fulfills the will of those who fear Him; וְאֶת שַׁוְעָתָם יִשְׁמַע וְיוֹשִׁיעֵם—and He hears their cries (in times of trouble) and He saves them. (That is for those who serve Hashem from fear (מיראה).)

שׁוֹמֵר יְהֹוָה אֶת כָּל אֹהֲבָיו—(But) those who serve Hashem from love (מאהבה), He will protect them from troubles in the first place! (Alternatively,) for those who serve Hashem from love (מאהבה), He reserves and preserves (שומר) their ultimate and eternal reward to be given in Olam Haba; וְאֵת כָּל הָרְשָׁעִים יַשְׁמִיד—and Hashem will destroy all evil.

תְּהִלַּת יְהֹוָה יְדַבֶּר פִּי—May my mouth declare the praises of Hashem (so powerfully and sincerely, that); וִיבָרֵךְ כָּל בָּשָׂר שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד—everyone (will be so impacted by my words and actions, that they too) will bless Hashem and see Him as the Source for all blessings—for eternity!

(And to sum up that entire Chapter 145 in one sentence:) וַאֲנַחְנוּ נְבָרֵךְ יָהּ—And each of us (in our way, based on our own life experiences,) will thank Hashem and see Him as the Source of blessing in our individual lives; מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם—now and forever (no matter what will happen! To sum it all up in one word:); הַלְלוּיָהּ—whatever happens, praise Hashem!

הַלְלוּיָהּ, הַלְלִי נַפְשִׁי—My very being praises Hashem! My entire lifestyle is a Kiddush Hashem! Do not put your ultimate faith in others, that they can solve all your problems and care for all your needs. They are mere mortals whose power is limited. (Even though we need mentors, friends, and family—no one can manage on their own, but) real happiness and security comes from realizing that in the end, it
is Hashem Who feeds (materially and spiritually) the hungry, and all is ultimately in His Hands.
—The Kingship of Hashem is for all eternity (thus we can be assured that He will always be there for us, unlike our mortal helpers);
—and Hashem has a special providence on Eretz Yisrael;
—in all generations, our past and our future;
—whatever happens, praise Hashem!

—As the Era of Mashiach dawns, and all confusion begins to clear, it will be pleasant and enjoyable to sing out and praise Hashem! Hashem is the builder of Yerushalayim, and He will gather in all the exiles, and heal all the broken bodies and souls. Hashem, Who controls the vastness of nature, views each individual Jew like a star, and each one is beloved by Hashem. Thus everyone will sing praises to Hashem. (Unlike now, in the Era of Mashiach) the borders of Eretz Yisrael will be secure, the gates of

Yerushalayim will be strong—we will realize that our true ultimate protection is from Hashem.
Such unique providence and miraculous continuity was not shown to any other nation; and only we are entrusted with His Torah and Divine laws (and therefore); whatever happens, praise Hashem!

In the Era of Mashiach, it will be evident to all that the Heavens and angels; the sun, moon, and stars; the great mountains, forests, oceans, and the entire animal kingdom—all praise Hashem! In addition, all the nations of the world—the rulers and the regular people—will recognize the power and providence of Hashem on nature and on us, His people.

(And how will all this come about? Because) Hashem will raise the glory of His nation (such that); תְּהִלָּה לְכָל חֲסִידָיו—everyone will praise His righteous ones (and who are His righteous ones?); לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַם קְרֹבוֹ—us, Bnei Yisrael (including me!) who stayed close to Hashem (when it was not easy and clear!); הַלְלוּיָהּ—(and therefore,) whatever happens, praise Hashem!

All will sing a new song of praise to Hashem; תְּהִלָּתוֹ בִּקְהַל חֲסִידִים—He will be praised by all righteous peoples. (But even in that new era) we, Bnei Yisrael, will be especially joyous, since Hashem had always been our King, and made us His unique nation (long before Mashiach's arrival). And Hashem has special favor for us since we showed our allegiance to His Torah (even when life was difficult and not clear)!

And in that era, Hashem will mete out the final punishments to all those nations who did evil, as is clearly foretold in the Torah; הָדָר הוּא לְכָל חֲסִידָיו—and bring everlasting glory to His righteous ones. (And therefore); הַלְלוּיָהּ—whatever happens, praise Hashem!

הַלְלוּיָהּ, הַלְלוּ אֵל בְּקָדְשׁוֹ—We proclaim the greatness of Hashem as seen by His acts that are above nature, and as seen by His providence within nature. We praise Hashem with every sort of musical instrument (meaning—with all our sometimes-conflicting thoughts, emotions, and no matter what mood we are in—at all times and in all circumstances—we sing out to Hashem, knowing that all is for our best).

כֹּל הַנְּשָׁמָה תְּהַלֵּל יָהּ—Every neshamah—every individual—should praise Hashem; our entire complex neshamah should, as one harmonious whole, praise Hashem; every breath we take (all that we do) should bring praise to Hashem. (And therefore); הַלְלוּיָהּ—whatever happens, praise Hashem!

בָּרוּךְ יְהֹוָה לְעוֹלָם אָמֵן וְאָמֵן—I am absolutely certain that Hashem is the Source of all that was and all that will be. בָּרוּךְ יְהֹוָה מִצִּיּוֹן, שֹׁכֵן יְרוּשָׁלָיִם—And that Hashem is the Source of our eternal connection to Eretz Yisrael and Yerushalayim. (And therefore); הַלְלוּיָהּ—whatever happens, praise Hashem! בָּרוּךְ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהִים אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל—Hashem, the Source of everything, Who has taken care of us, Bnei Yisrael; עֹשֵׂה נִפְלָאוֹת לְבַדּוֹ—He alone performs wonderous miracles.

וּבָרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹדוֹ לְעוֹלָם—And may the perception of Hashem's Presence be increased forever; וְיִמָּלֵא כְבוֹדוֹ אֶת כָּל הָאָרֶץ—and may the perception of Hashem's Presence be felt by everyone, over the entire earth. אָמֵן וְאָמֵן—This is the absolute truth, and I hope it will happen soon!

David HaMelech proclaims publicly: Hashem—You are the Source of everything (that I have achieved)—all greatness, power, wealth, and rulership is Yours, Hashem. You have the power to give us the strength (to become great and fulfill our mission). And we thank You for all You have done!

אַתָּה הוּא—The Navi Nechemiah proclaims: You, Hashem, alone, created the entire universe, and You chose Avraham! You saved him from Ur Kasdim;

וְכָרוֹת עִמּוֹ הַבְּרִית—and You established an everlasting covenant with him to give Eretz Yisrael to his descendants (that's us!). You saw the suffering of Bnei Yisrael in Egypt, and You performed great public miracles—culminating with splitting the sea in order to save us, Your nation (for a great mission to the world).

וַיּוֹשַׁע—On that day Hashem rescued Bnei Yisrael from Egypt, and Bnei Yisrael personally saw all the Egyptians dead on the seashore. Bnei Yisrael saw the great power that Hashem unleashed against Egypt; the people were in awe of Hashem; they trusted Hashem and believed in His servant Moshe.

אָז יָשִׁיר מֹשֶׁה—Then Moshe and Bnei Yisrael chose to sing this Shirah to Hashem and said: I will sing to Hashem for He has triumphed over the haughty (Egyptians); His strength and power saved me. This is my God (I will create my own personal relationship with Hashem); and He is the God of my father (and that unique relationship will be built on the foundations of our ancestors). Hashem cast Pharaoh's chariots and army into the sea and they all drowned; at the same time the flowing waters stood like walls (to save us). The enemy said,

מִי כָמֹכָה בָּאֵלִם יְהֹוָה—Among all the powers (powers of nature, powers of humans), who is equal to You, Hashem?; מִי כָּמֹכָה נֶאְדָּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ—Who is like You, powerful but with purity of purpose?; נוֹרָא תְהִלֹּת עֹשֵׂה פֶלֶא—Our songs praising You instill in us awe of Your wondrous deeds, which are in truth beyond our comprehension. All the nations of the world shuddered with fear (when they heard of this great miracle). May dread and fear fall upon them until Your nation crosses over (into Eretz Yisrael), the place Your Presence is most felt.
(Just as we have seen the rulership of Hashem here at the sea, so too for all future times) Hashem will reign forever and ever!

(Once Mashiach comes) the entire world will recognize Hashem as the King of His nation, Bnei Yisrael, and the ruler over all nations. On that day, Hashem will be recognized as the sole power, and His Presence will be felt by all.

Hashem our King, Who is קדוש (above all rules of nature) and is King of the entire Heavens and earth, May the impact of all You do (שמך) be praised forever. For specifically to You, Hashem, Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout history, is it fitting to offer all praises and thanksgiving, now and forever.

You, —בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, Hashem, are the Source of everything; אֵל מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל —all-powerful בַּתִּשְׁבָּחוֹת King Who is greater than any praises (that we mere humans can say); אֵל הַהוֹדָאוֹת —to Whom all thanksgiving is due; אֲדוֹן הַנִּפְלָאוֹת —Master of wonders; הַבּוֹחֵר בְּשִׁירֵי —Who takes pleasure זִמְרָה in songs of praise; מֶלֶךְ אֵל חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים —You are the King Who gives life to the world.

The focus of this chapter is that even when we are מִמַּעֲמַקִּים— (note that it is plural, meaning "depths") experiencing either the depths of misfortune and difficulties or the depths of feelings of guilt because we know we have messed up; no matter what, we can turn to Hashem because He is full of chessed, and וְהַרְבֵּה עִמּוֹ פְדוּת —His power to redeem and forgive us is great.

Instant Insight: The first letters of the first four words of this chapter, מזמור שיר חנוכת הבית (which discusses all of David HaMelech's difficulties) spell out שמחה. True, deep simchah is based on rock-solid belief that in the end all is for the best and a Beis Hamikdash will result! (Even though we cannot always see the sense of Hashem's plan, hinted to by the fact that the letters are not in order.)
הֲרֵינִי מְזַמֵּן אֶת פִּי לְהוֹדוֹת וּלְהַלֵּל וּלְשַׁבֵּחַ אֶת בּוֹרְאִי לְשֵׁם יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּהּ עַל יְדֵי הַהוּא טָמִיר וְנֶעְלָם בְּשֵׁם כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל.

FAQ: But how am I supposed to now sing all these praises to Hashem when my life is so difficult? I have so much stuff going on, and it's hard to accept that all is fair and just! ANSWER: That is the classic question of "tzaddik v'ra lo"—why the righteous suffer"! See Appendix 2.
Since Hodu is very long and a collection of various pesukim and statements (rather than being one chapter of Tehillim), we are going to break it up into sections and focus on a few key phrases.
NOTE: Even if rushed, it is best to not skip this tefillah because of its importance. Therefore, every pasuk is explained.
Omit on Erev Pesach, Chol Hamoed Pesach, and Erev Yom Kippur.

Why do we say Mizmor L'Sodah daily when the original Korban Todah was brought only when a person miraculously survived some life-threatening situation (like when we "bentch gomel" today)? In truth, every minute of our day is a miracle—we just don't realize it! To demand that every individual go to the Beis Hamikdash every day and offer a Korban Todah is too great a burden. But now that tefillah has taken the place of korbanos, we say Mizmor L'Sodah daily to make us appreciate the "natural" miracles we take for granted.

Since this is really about the Korban Todah, why is it not in the section of Korbanos? The answer is that this korban is very different. The Midrash tells us that when Mashiach comes, the only personal voluntary korban that will be brought will be the Korban Todah. Why? Because even when Mashiach comes, it will still be a struggle for us not to take for granted all the good we have!

It is so hard to "serve Hashem with happiness and peace of mind (בשמחה)" when our lives seem so difficult! The key—the word בשמחה rearranged spells the word מחשבה—thinking. Happiness and peace of mind does not happen by itself. It comes from choosing to look at your life from a certain perspective. If you put your mind (מחשבה) to it—you can have peace of mind (בשמחה)!

Answer: Complex and deep question! See Appendix 5.

Instant Insight: We are referred to as the "עַם סְגֻלָּה—special treasure" of Hashem. The word segulah is related to the word "segol"—the three-dot triangle nekudah that appears under letters (that makes the "eh" sound). No matter which way you turn the segol, it remains the very same shape—the same segol. Similarly, Bnei Yisrael, no matter where we are or what choices we might make, we are always the unique nation of Hashem. We cannot escape that, and He will not let us go.

Instant Insight:
There is no נ in Ashrei—why? The Maharal says that these pesukim, starting with the letters of the aleph-beis, express the inherent meaning (based on Kabbalah) of those letters. The inherent meaning of נ is נפילה—a falling. Here David HaMelech is describing what Hashem does, and Hashem does not cause our fallings! Our mistakes are the result of our own poor choices! In the next verse we are told what Hashem does in regard to our fallings—סוֹמֵךְ יְהֹוָה לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים—He helps us get back up!

Crucial Instant Insight:
It does not say that Hashem is close to all "קראחו באמת"—who now call to Him with honesty and integrity. Rather, "אשר יקראהו באמת"—who will call to Him with honesty, in the future tense. This means that if right now you have a very "up and down" relationship with Hashem; and you struggle with being 100 percent sincere, 100 percent of the time, and at times you are a bit of a hypocrite as far as what you promise Hashem and what you end up doing—still, as long as you are committed to being "יקראהו באמת"—your goal is to be completely sincere, honest, and genuine in your relationship with Hashem—then already now He will listen to Your requests for help to get there!
The focus of this chapter is on the individual—each person praises Hashem in their own way and through their own life; and Hashem's providence is on each individual in the world.

The focus of this chapter is on Am Yisrael as a whole, and on the dawn of Era of Mashiach—when the power and providence of Hashem in our individual and national lives will finally begin to become clear.

בּוֹנֵה יְרוּשָׁלָֽם literally translates as, "Hashem is building Yerushalayim"—present tense—even though in context it is referring to the Era of Mashiach. That is telling us that in truth, every single thing that happened and happens to us as individuals and as a nation is part of the process needed to build Yerushalayim. Thus all through our galus, all that Hashem has sent our way is part of a continuous building of Yerushalayim. Once Mashiach comes, that will all be clear.
תהילים קמח
This chapter, the very last chapter of the book of Tehillim, sums up the previous chapters.

Instant Insight: The first letters of the opening four words—ויברך—spell דוד את ה', "ודאי," one of the Names of Hashem, which represents His attribute of certainty and reliability. Notwithstanding all the difficulties in his life, David HaMelech always lived with the belief that Hashem can be relied on to take care of him.
